agent_requirement.reason: Agents generating or modifying Go must run gofmt + golangci-lint before declaring work complete — formatting and lint violations caught at write time, not review time
agent_requirement.how: gofmt -w <file> && golangci-lint run <file> — fix all errors; suppress only with a //nolint:<linter> comment and a rationale

claude_code.scope_reason:
Owner ruling 2026-07-25: LSP plugins are a per-machine setting (~/.claude/settings.json), and every enabled plugin is a real background process + a line in every session's plugin manifest -- not free. Go isn't in broad use across this org's repos yet (unlike TypeScript/Python, enabled at the user level as defaults), so gopls-lsp should be enabled per-project (that repo's own .claude/settings.json), not user-wide. A project's settings.json layers on top of the user's, so this adds gopls without touching the global default:
  { "enabledPlugins": { "gopls-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true } }
claude_code.note: gopls is the official Go team language server -- covers formatting-on type info, hover, goToDefinition, documentSymbol. It does not replace golangci-lint; both stay in the pre-push/CI gate.

complexity.note: Matches node.yaml's floor for consistency across languages. Not yet validated against a real Go codebase in this org -- adopted as a sane cross-language default. gocyclo and cyclop measure slightly different things (cyclomatic vs cognitive complexity); either is acceptable, cyclop is the closer analogue to Biome's cognitive-complexity check.
